subject: math
title: Long Division
seo_title: Grade 4 Long Division Worksheets: Remainders, Zeros in the Quotient and Word Problems
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 long division worksheets: divide up to 4-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers, remainders, zeros in the quotient, area models and word problems that use the remainder. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Repeat until every digit is used.
key_sub: Start with the biggest place. If the divisor does not fit, write 0. The remainder is always less than the divisor. Check: quotient × divisor + remainder = dividend.
body_html:
Divide one place at a time

To divide a big number, split it into hundreds, tens and ones and divide each part. Then add the answers. An area model shows this: the divisor is the side, the dividend is the area.

Long division: 4 steps

Long division does the same thing in a short layout. Start with the biggest place and repeat four steps.

StepWhat you do
1. DivideHow many times does the divisor fit?
2. MultiplyQuotient digit × divisor
3. SubtractThe difference must be less than the divisor
4. Bring downWrite the next digit next to the difference, then divide again

Remainders

The remainder is what is left when nothing more can be shared. It is always less than the divisor. Write it with R: 857 ÷ 6 = 142 R 5. Check: quotient × divisor + remainder = dividend. 142 × 6 + 5 = 857.

Zeros in the quotient

If the divisor does not fit, write 0 in the quotient and bring down the next digit. Never skip a place.

Word problems: what does the remainder mean?

The question asksUse the remainder like this125 people, 8 in each van: 125 ÷ 8 = 15 R 5
How many are needed for everyone?Add 1 to the quotient16 vans
How many full groups?Leave the remainder out15 full vans
How many are left over?The remainder is the answer5 people

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Skipping a zero (4,218 ÷ 6 = 73)When the divisor does not fit, write 0 in the quotient
A remainder bigger than the divisor (85 ÷ 6 = 13 R 7)If the difference is the divisor or more, the divisor fits one more time
Forgetting to bring down a digitEvery digit of the dividend needs a digit above it in the quotient
Ignoring the remainder in a word problemAsk: do the leftovers need one more van, box or table?

faq.q: How do you teach long division to a 4th grader?
faq.a: Teach four repeating steps: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Start with an area model or place-value sharing so the steps make sense, then move to the long division layout.

faq.q: Why is there a 0 in the quotient of 4,218 ÷ 6?
faq.a: After dividing 42 hundreds, you bring down the 1 ten. 6 does not fit into 1, so the quotient has 0 tens. Without the 0, the answer would be 73 instead of 703.

faq.q: How do you check a division answer with a remainder?
faq.a: Multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder. You should get the dividend: for 857 ÷ 6 = 142 R 5, 142 × 6 + 5 = 857.
It is the Common Core standard for Grade 4: divide numbers up to four digits by one-digit numbers, find quotients and remainders, and explain the work with equations, arrays or area models.

sets.title: Word problems: what to do with the remainder

items.q: There are 365 days in a year. How many full weeks are in a year?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 7, so start with 36. 36 ÷ 7 = 5, 5 × 7 = 35, 36 − 35 = 1. Bring down 5: 15 ÷ 7 = 2, 2 × 7 = 14, 15 − 14 = 1. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 1. So 365 ÷ 7 = 52 R 1. Check: 52 × 7 + 1 = 365. The 1 day left over is not enough to make another week, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 52 weeks.

items.q: A factory has 3,263 crayons. It puts 8 crayons in each box. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 8, so start with 32. 32 ÷ 8 = 4, 4 × 8 = 32, 32 − 32 = 0. Bring down 6: 6 ÷ 8 = 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 3: 63 ÷ 8 = 7, 7 × 8 = 56, 63 − 56 = 7. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 7. So 3,263 ÷ 8 = 407 R 7. Check: 407 × 8 + 7 = 3,263. The 7 crayons left over are not enough to fill another box, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 407 boxes.

items.q: A farm collected 1,017 eggs. Each carton holds 6 eggs. How many cartons are needed to hold all the eggs?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 6, so start with 10. 10 ÷ 6 = 1, 1 × 6 = 6, 10 − 6 = 4. Bring down 1: 41 ÷ 6 = 6, 6 × 6 = 36, 41 − 36 = 5. Bring down 7: 57 ÷ 6 = 9, 9 × 6 = 54, 57 − 54 = 3. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 1,017 ÷ 6 = 169 R 3. Check: 169 × 6 + 3 = 1,017. 169 cartons are not enough: 3 eggs still need a carton. Add 1 more, so the answer is 170 cartons.

So 123 ÷ 7 = 17 R 4. Check: 17 × 7 + 4 = 123. The 4 students left over are not enough to make another team, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 17 teams.

So 196 ÷ 8 = 24 R 4. Check: 24 × 8 + 4 = 196. 24 vans are not enough: 4 people still need a van. Add 1 more, so the answer is 25 vans.

Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 1,851 ÷ 8 = 231 R 3. Check: 231 × 8 + 3 = 1,851. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 3 cookies.

items.q: There are 70 campers going on an overnight trip. Each tent sleeps 4 campers. How many tents are needed?
items.e: Divide: 7 ÷ 4 = 1, 1 × 4 = 4, 7 − 4 = 3. Bring down 0: 30 ÷ 4 = 7, 7 × 4 = 28, 30 − 28 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 70 ÷ 4 = 17 R 2. Check: 17 × 4 + 2 = 70. 17 tents are not enough: 2 campers still need a tent. Add 1 more, so the answer is 18 tents.

items.q: Nora has a ribbon that is 146 inches long. She cuts it into pieces that are each 6 inches long. How many pieces can she cut?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 6, so start with 14. 14 ÷ 6 = 2, 2 × 6 = 12, 14 − 12 = 2. Bring down 6: 26 ÷ 6 = 4, 4 × 6 = 24, 26 − 24 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 146 ÷ 6 = 24 R 2. Check: 24 × 6 + 2 = 146. The 2 inches left over are not enough to cut another piece, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 24 pieces.

items.q: An orchard picked 1,071 apples. The apples are packed in bags of 8. How many full bags can be packed?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 8, so start with 10. 10 ÷ 8 = 1, 1 × 8 = 8, 10 − 8 = 2. Bring down 7: 27 ÷ 8 = 3, 3 × 8 = 24, 27 − 24 = 3. Bring down 1: 31 ÷ 8 = 3, 3 × 8 = 24, 31 − 24 = 7. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 7. So 1,071 ÷ 8 = 133 R 7. Check: 133 × 8 + 7 = 1,071. The 7 apples left over are not enough to fill another bag, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 133 bags.

items.q: Eli shares 64 stickers equally among 6 friends. Each friend gets as many as possible. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: Divide: 6 ÷ 6 = 1, 1 × 6 = 6, 6 − 6 = 0. Bring down 4: 4 ÷ 6 = 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 4. So 64 ÷ 6 = 10 R 4. Check: 10 × 6 + 4 = 64. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 4 stickers.
